basis: T3 (decisions.md D4): Applied Materials went public in 1972 (Wikipedia), the year Kleiner Perkins was founded, and no source names a Kleiner Perkins round before that listing; the firm's only trace is a nameless tile on the 2021-24 logo grid and a press line that Tom Perkins was 'associated with' the company, so any position was taken in a listed company.

T3 (decisions.md D4): DMX Technologies listed on the Singapore Exchange in 2002 (GMT Research; its share option scheme dates from 2002-11-12), five years before KPCB China's first fund (2007), so a KPCB China fund can only have bought into a listed company; KDDI's release of 2009-09-10 names Venture Corporation and management as the major holders and no Kleiner Perkins vehicle, and no private round is on record. The same reading as CASI.

Listed on the firm's own portfolio site (2010, 2012), and the T3 check passes: Murugan Capital, described as KPCB's wholly owned subsidiary, held Info Edge shares bought at Rs. 245 each according to the company's red herring prospectus (the 2006 IPO document), beside Sherpalo's own Mauritius vehicle, and sold 1.55% of the equity on 2010-03-12 (MediaNama 2010-03-16). A pre-IPO purchase by the firm's own vehicle, not a joint vehicle (R3) and not a market purchase.

note: A/B pass: KPCB's vehicle Murugan Capital bought Info Edge shares at Rs. 245 each before the November 2006 listing, as the red herring prospectus records (MediaNama 2010-03-16), a pre-IPO purchase in an eleven-year-old company, so Growth, dated by the prospectus year; it sold most of the stake in March 2010, which is why the firm's 2012 page reads Acquired. The T3 question is closed.
